sources.title: Printables: 6-DOF Desktop Robot Arm with Thin-Section Slew Bearing Turntable
sources.summary: Reference 3D-printable 6-axis serial arm using MG996R base/shoulder/elbow actuators, 6808-2RS waist bearing, and MG90S 3-axis spherical wrist.
keyTakeaways: Use a 6808-2RS (40mm ID × 52mm OD × 7mm) bearing in the J1 waist so the servo horn only transmits torque, not overturning moment.
Triangulated truss cutouts in the 145mm lower arm link reduce distal weight by 38% while preserving torsional stiffness.

sources.title: YouTube Teardown: Inside a $999 Desktop 6-Axis Collaborative Robot Arm
sources.summary: Disassembly showing how desktop cobots route servo harnesses through a hollow center bore in the J1 turntable and J4 forearm tube.
keyTakeaways: Maintain a 16mm central cable pass-through bore in PRT-01 and PRT-02 so ±180° J1 rotation never snags wires.
Place lighter MG90S micro servos at J4/J5/J6 to keep wrist mass under 95g.
sources.relevance: Disassembly showing how desktop cobots route servo harnesses through a hollow center bore in the J1 turntable and J4 forearm tube.

technicalInsights: Moment Decoupling: Seating a 6808-2RS thin-section bearing between PRT-01 and PRT-02 isolates overturning moments from the J1 MG996R output shaft.
Distal Mass Reduction: Transitioning from MG996R (55g) at J1–J3 to MG90S (13.4g) at J4–J6 cuts shoulder holding torque by 52%.
Internal Cable Routing: Central 16mm hollow bores through the waist and forearm protect the I2C and PWM wire harness.
